criteria.no: A decisive term is a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term can be understood from the statement or common technical knowledge.

self_contained.instructions: Can each decisive term in `anchor.statement` be understood from the statement itself or from common technical knowledge? Understood terms include commands, subcommands, flags, files, paths, values, environment variables, formats, streams, roles such as 'the caller', and terms the statement defines inline. Bundled duties, added details, sentence form, and who is told to act (a named component, 'you', or nobody) do not matter here. A term cannot be understood when it is a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record. Judge each decisive term separately: one undefined label, tier, or mode, or one subjective quality, makes the answer no even when the statement also names many concrete paths, hashes, codes, or ids.

anchor.statement: The pkg sync-lock command must rewrite package.lock so that its entries are sorted by package name.
anchor.quote: pkg sync-lock has to rewrite package.lock with entries sorted by package name
